explanation:
Let, P(t2, 2t) be any point on the parabola y2 = 4x. C be the mirror image of the parabola y2 = 4x with respect to the line UV : x + y + 4 = 0.

The curve C cuts the line KL : y = 5 at A and B.

Let, B(, ) be the image of the point P(t2, 2t).

Clearly, PB UV and PQ = QB.

or, ...... (1)

The point of intersection of the lines UV and KL is R.

Let us join P and R.

From PQR and BQR,

(i) BQ = PQ [ B is the image of P]

(ii) PQR = RQB = 90 [ PB UV]

(iii) QR common

PQR BQR [by SAS congruence criterion]

QRP = BRQ [CPCT]

slope of x + y + 4 = 0 is 1,

UTO = 135

OTR = 45

Again, X'X || KL and UV transversal.

OTR = TRB = 45 BRQ = QRP = 45

PRB = 90 PR KL

coordinates of R are (t2, ).

the point R lies on KL,

= 5

Again, the point R lies on the straight line x + y + 4 = 0.

t2 + + 4 = 0

or, t2 5 + 4 = 0 [ = 5]

or, t2 = 1 or, t = 1

when t = 1, = 5, then (1) 1 = 5 2 or = 6

when, t = 1, = 5, then (1) 1 = 5 + 2 or, = 2

So, the coordinates of A and B are (6, 5) and (2, 5) respectively.

AB = 4 units

So, the distance between A and B is 4 units.
